chapter: Touring in the bus years and Jim Crow in the South
title: Miami: Russell Embray shoved, and Iller barred from the Black cab
summary: Lead trumpeter Embray is pushed off the sidewalk and white band manager Iller has trouble riding to the Black hotel and the Esquire Club.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Was Artis Paul with you then?
No, Artis wasn't with me right then. We'll get to Artis. I'll tell you who was with us then; did you know Russell Embray?
I worked with Artis Paul and Russell Embray.
Russell Embray from Wichita, Kansas was in the band then and we went on the train and so when we got off--
I think we should spell Embray, E-M-B=R-A-Y, Russell Embray, a great lead trumpet player from Wichita.

So we got off the train and you know there's a tendency to go to the right when you meet anybody, and Embray was meeting a policeman and his right was the wall of the station, so there wasn't anywhere for him to go. So when he met this officer--this is in Miami--when he met this officer, he didn't hit him like that with his billy, but it pushed him in the side and said, nigger, get off of the sidewalk, you must be one of those smart niggers from up north. When you meet a white man, get off of the sidewalk.

And so we walked on then and Iller was with us then, this white boy, so we had and we headed toward this black cab, and so whoever got in first got in and so when Iller went to get him, the driver said, I can't hold you and he said I'm the band manager, I've got to go with them, I got to get them checked into the hotel. He said I can't lose my license because you're the band manager and so I said I'll get you a yellow, I know where we're going,

I've been there before. So I gave him the address of the hotel. When we got to the hotel, he comes in there, the people say he can't stay there; so I sent him on downtown and we were playing a very nice club there in Miami, the Esquire Club, Jews only.
It was a black club but white owned--
Yes, the white owned it. Unless maybe black had it before, but white owned it.

So anyway, Iller said to them I don't know what I'm going to do tonight, it looks like I'm just a headache to you, Ernie. I said what's wrong? He said, well--I said did you get a room? Yeah, but I don't know how I'm going to get on. I said what are you talking about? He said the white cab driver said they don't like him to come over here after twelve o'clock.
